cells.quote: The review reports, citing Koedinger et al. (2010), a quasi-experimental comparison of students using vs. not using a formative assessment mathematics tool, with outcomes on a standardized mathematics test.
cells.note: No study-text passage reporting this specific comparison or its direction is included above; quote taken from the wiki entry.

O.outcome_detail: association with mentality measured by median mental age and IQ

cells.quote: The association coefficient, Q, for the relation of the four classes, School Retarded and Below Median in Mentality, School Retarded and Above Median in Mentality, School Advanced and Below Median in Mentality, School Advanced and Above Median in Mentality, was found to be +.85.
cells.note: The study reports a measured association, not an instructional treatment.

O.outcome_detail: association with mental diagnosis based on IQ

cells.quote: Q, for the classes, 'School Retarded and Mentally Backward or Below, School Retarded and Mentally Bright or Above, School Advanced and Mentally Backward or Below, School Advanped and Mentally Bright or Above, was found to be +.97.
cells.note: Normal school and normal mentality groups were eliminated for this coefficient.

D.treatment: four or more grades retarded in school
D.comparison: more than one grade advanced in school

cells.quote: Four grades or more retarded in school is a perfect indication of a mentality not higher than normal, with the chances greatly in favor of its indicating at least a backward mentality. Two grades or more advanced in school are likewise a perfect indication of at least a normal mentality, with the chances greatly in favor of its indicating at least a bright diagnosis.
cells.note: The perfect association was obtained after selecting limiting values for school retardation/advancement and mentality.

O.outcome_detail: association between school progress and mentality

result.effect: School A had the lowest Q-values; no single printed coefficient

cells.quote: School A consistently has the lowest Q-values of the three schools, such as we might be led to expect where the standards are changing the most rapidly from grade to grade.
cells.note: School A was of highest social status and School C of lowest social status; the text reports a comparative pattern rather than one numerical effect.

result.effect: 2D mean 5.19 (±2.12) vs 3D mean 5.45 (±2.16); p < 0.0001 for non-inferiority; p = 0.215 for mean-score difference

cells.quote: The 2D group had a mean score of 5.19 (± 2.12), whereas the 3D group had a mean score of 5.45 (± 2.16). The findings of the 3D group were not significantly inferior to those of the 2D group (p < 0.0001).
cells.note: The study text also reports: “3D presentation was statistically non-inferior to 2D (p < 0.0001); no significant difference between mean scores (p = 0.215).” Because no equivalence test or adequate power is reported, direction is coded ns rather than 0.

O.outcome_detail: academic, behavioral, social-emotional, and motivational outcomes; pooled across most outcomes

cells.quote: Finally, most recently, Kopershoek and colleagues (2016) conducted a rigorous meta-analysis of 54 interventions appearing between 2003 and 2013 examining the effects of classroom management programs, including those that focused solely on developing positive teacher-student relationships and students’ social-emotional learning, on primary school students’ academic, behavioral, social-emotional and motivational outcomes. This meta-analysis suggested that primary school classroom management programs had a small, statistically significant effect (g = 0.08 to 0.39) on most outcomes, with stronger effects emerging for interventions focused on social-emotional development and teacher development.
cells.note: This is a report within the study's literature review of the Korpershoek et al. (2016) meta-analysis, not a new result from the Patall et al. synthesis.
